mechanism_claims.claim_text: DN59 directly disrupts dengue virions and promotes release/exposure of viral RNA genome rather than acting only as a reversible entry blocker.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: DN59 peptide against mature dengue virus particles
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper supports virion disruption/genome release for DN59; it does not define an antimicrobial bacterial membrane mechanism or an in vivo therapeutic mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: DN59 interacts with lipid vesicles and disrupts vesicle membrane integrity in vitro, supporting a membrane-disruption mechanism context for virion genome release.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: DN59 with POPC and POPC/POPG model vesicles

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=12:Lipid Vesicle Binding by Tryptophan Fluorescence

mechanism_claims.limitations: Model-vesicle leakage supports membrane interaction but is not by itself a cellular toxicity endpoint.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Time-of-addition and cell-treatment controls support a virion-directed mechanism: DN59 did not show inhibition when applied to cells before virus addition or after infection in the source-controlled experiments.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Supplemental Figure S1 images are TIFF assets; the XML caption supports the qualitative controls, while exact plotted values were not extracted.
